title: Maximum Innovation Grants Allocation
real_world_story: An enterprise internal incubator committee has a discretionary grassroots innovation budget of B thousand dollars. N employee teams have submitted grant proposals, each requesting an exact fixed seed grant of g_i thousand dollars. To promote a culture of widespread experimentation across the company, the committee's objective is to fund the maximum possible number of distinct innovation proposals without exceeding the total budget B.
problem_statement: Given budget B and an array of N grant request amounts g_1, g_2, ..., g_N, determine the maximum number of proposals that can be completely funded within budget B.
task: Compute and print the maximum count of distinct proposals that can be funded.
input_format:
The first line contains two space-separated integers N and B, the number of proposals and the total grant budget.
The second line contains N space-separated integers g_1, g_2, ..., g_N, representing the grant amounts requested.
output_format: Print a single integer representing the maximum number of proposals that can be funded.

examples.explanation: Sorting grant amounts in ascending order: [10, 20, 30, 40, 50]. Cumulative sum: 10 + 20 + 30 + 40 = 100 <= 100. Adding the next proposal (50) would exceed the budget (150 > 100). Maximum proposals funded = 4.
Funding 1 proposal costs 10 <= 15. Funding 2 proposals would cost 20 > 15. Maximum funded = 1.

real_world_takeaway: Greedy selection of lowest-cost requests provably maximizes the cardinality of satisfied projects within a bounded financial endowment.
